key_facts: COMSPOC research found typical satellite operators may only be retiring 7 percent of actual collision risk, leaving 93 percent unmitigated.
Low-confidence space situational awareness data can make genuine collision risks appear minimal, while also generating excessive false-alarm warnings.
COMSPOC's analysis indicates substantial improvements in orbital positional accuracy are achievable with commercially available software and data.
The author argues success in space domain awareness should be measured by decision confidence rather than number of observations, network size, or customer count.
Dan Oltrogge is COMSPOC's Chief Scientist and Director of the Center for Space Standards and Innovation.
